public_rationale: The June 1, 2023 preprint evaluated GPT-3, ChatGPT and GPT-4 on multiplication, logic grid puzzles and dynamic programming, finding sharply declining performance as compositional complexity increased [e1]. These results support systematic reasoning limitations in those models and tasks [e1]. Anthropic's August 8, 2023 report found more abstract and stronger cross-language generalization with model size, limiting a literal pure-memorization reading of the metaphor [e2].
limitations: The tested models and tasks do not establish that every neural architecture lacks systematic reasoning [e1].
The evidence does not establish that model outputs are merely memorized fragments [e2].
The normative standard of how systematic reasoning machines ought to be is not measured by these studies [e1, e2].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Popular neural networks still struggle with systematic relational reasoning and are not as systematic as reasoning machines should be.

statement.excerpt: Forty one years later, neural networks (at least of the popular variety) still struggle with this. They still remain pointillistic masses of blurry memory, never as systematic as reasoning machines ought to be.
statement.document_title: Elegant and powerful new result that seriously undermines large language models

from_speaker: at least of the popular variety

our_interpretation: Assess the empirical assertion that contemporary popular neural models have substantial failures of systematic relational and compositional reasoning.
The metaphor about blurry memory and the standard expressed by ought are not separately measurable claims.
Because model evaluations have no fixed quarterly reporting cycle, use the latest annual evaluation period available before the post: 2023, restricted to work preceding September 22.
criteria.support_condition: Controlled evaluations of contemporary widely used neural models show substantial failures when combining or transferring learned relationships and reasoning operations.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Relevant controlled evaluations show consistently reliable systematic transfer, with the alleged failures absent or attributable to invalid tests.

evidence.explanation: The study evaluates GPT-3, ChatGPT and GPT-4 on multiplication, relational logic puzzles and dynamic programming. Performance deteriorates sharply as compositional complexity increases, supporting the claim that popular models struggle with systematic reasoning.

The researchers find increasingly abstract and cross-language generalization as models grow. This limits a literal interpretation that neural models are only stores of memorized fragments; it does not negate demonstrated systematicity failures.
